title: Perimeter & Area Review, Arc Lengths & Sector Area: Angular Proportionality
description: Master the angular fraction principle connecting central angle θ to circumference and area. Rigorously derive Arc Length l = (θ/360) × 2πr and Sector Area A = (θ/360) × πr² = 1/2 × l × r. Understand minor sectors, major sectors, and quadrants.
key_concepts: Angular Fraction Principle: Since a full circle corresponds to 360°, a central angle of θ corresponds to the fractional part θ / 360°
Arc Length Formula: l = (θ / 360°) × 2πr
Area of Sector Formula: Area = (θ / 360°) × πr²
Kinetic Sector Relation: Area of sector = 1/2 × (Arc length) × Radius = 1/2 × l × r (Analogous to 1/2 × base × height!)
Major Sector: Area of Major Sector = πr² - Area of Minor Sector = [ (360° - θ) / 360° ] × πr²
Quadrant of a Circle: Sector with central angle θ = 90° ⇒ Area = 1/4 πr²
subtopics: Full derivation of arc length and sector area formulas
Connecting clock minute hand rotations to central angles (360° in 60 min ⇒ 6° per min)
Worked Example 1 and Example 2 from NCERT

worked_examples.given: Radius of circle r = 4 cm. Angle of minor sector θ = 30°. Value of π = 3.14 (Fig. 11.4).
worked_examples.formula:
1. Area of minor sector = (θ / 360°) × πr²
2. Area of major sector = πr² - Area of minor sector (or ((360° - θ) / 360°) × πr²).
worked_examples.finalAnswer: Minor sector area = 4.19 cm², Major sector area = 46.05 cm²
worked_examples.solution:
GIVEN:
Radius of the circle, r = 4 cm.
Sector angle, θ = 30°.
Use π = 3.14 (Fig. 11.4).

TO FIND:
(i) Area of the minor sector.
(ii) Area of the corresponding major sector.

FORMULA USED:
- Area of minor sector = (θ / 360°) × πr²
- Area of major sector = πr² - Area of minor sector, or ((360° - θ) / 360°) × πr².

STEP-BY-STEP CALCULATION:
Step 1: Compute Area of Minor Sector:
Area = (θ / 360°) × πr²
Area = (30° / 360°) × 3.14 × 4²
Area = (1 / 12) × 3.14 × 16
Area = (4 / 3) × 3.14 = 12.56 / 3 ≈ 4.19 cm².

Step 2: Compute Area of Major Sector:
Angle of major sector = 360° - 30° = 330°.
Area of major sector = (330° / 360°) × πr²
Area = (11 / 12) × 3.14 × 16
Area = (11 × 50.24) / 12 = 552.64 / 12 ≈ 46.05 cm².
(Alternatively: Area of circle - Area of minor sector = 50.24 - 4.19 = 46.05 cm²).

[ROUGH_WORK]
Total circle area = 3.14 × 16 = 50.24 cm². Minor fraction = 30/360 = 1/12. 50.24 / 12 = 4.186 ≈ 4.19. Major = 50.24 - 4.19 = 46.05 cm².
Boxed Answer: [ Minor Sector = 4.19 cm², Major Sector = 46.05 cm² ].
concept_questions: Why does the sum of the angles of the minor sector and the major sector always equal 360°?
Can the major sector area ever be smaller than the minor sector area?

title: Area of Segments: Sector-Triangle Decomposition for 60°, 90° & 120° Angles
description: Master the fundamental geometric decomposition for finding the area of a segment of a circle: Area of Segment = Area of Sector - Area of Triangle OAB. Learn the three standard central angle cases: θ = 60° (Equilateral triangle √3/4 r²), θ = 90° (Right-angled triangle 1/2 r²), and θ = 120° (Isosceles triangle √3/4 r²).
key_concepts: Segment Definition: A circular segment is a region bounded by a chord and the corresponding arc
Fundamental Area Formula: Area of Minor Segment = Area of Sector OAB - Area of Triangle OAB
Major Segment: Area of Major Segment = Area of Circle - Area of Minor Segment
Case 1 (θ = 60°): Since OA = OB = r and ∠AOB = 60°, ΔOAB is equilateral! Area(ΔOAB) = (√3 / 4) r²
Case 2 (θ = 90°): ΔOAB is a right-angled isosceles triangle with legs r and r. Area(ΔOAB) = 1/2 × r × r = 1/2 r²
Case 3 (θ = 120°): Drop perpendicular OM ⊥ AB. OM = r cos 60° = r/2, AB = 2r sin 60° = r√3. Area(ΔOAB) = 1/2 × AB × OM = 1/2 × r√3 × r/2 = (√3 / 4) r²!
subtopics: Geometric proof of triangle area for 60°, 90°, and 120°
Equilateral triangle derivation and altitude properties

worked_examples.given: Radius of circle r = 21 cm. Central angle ∠AOB = 120° (Fig. 11.6). Minor segment is bounded by chord AB and arc AYB.
worked_examples.formula:
Area of segment AYB = Area of sector OAYB - Area of ΔOAB.
Area of sector OAYB = (θ/360°) × πr².
Area of ΔOAB with central angle 120° = (1/2) × base × height = (1/2) × r² × sin(120°) = (1/2) × r² × (√3/2) = (√3/4) × r².
worked_examples.solution:
GIVEN:
Radius of the circle, r = 21 cm.
Central angle subtended by chord AB, ∠AOB = 120° (Fig. 11.6).
Use π = 22/7.

TO FIND:
Area of the segment AYB.

FORMULA USED:
Area of segment AYB = Area of sector OAYB - Area of ΔOAB.
- Area of sector OAYB = (θ / 360°) × πr²
- Area of ΔOAB = (1/2) × base × height = (1/2) × AB × OM (where OM ⊥ AB).

STEP-BY-STEP CALCULATION:
Step 1: Calculate the Area of sector OAYB:
Area of sector = (120° / 360°) × (22 / 7) × 21²
Area of sector = (1 / 3) × (22 / 7) × 441
Since 441 / 21 = 21:
Area of sector = (1 / 3) × 22 × 63 = 22 × 21 = 462 cm².

Step 2: Calculate the Area of ΔOAB:
Draw OM ⊥ AB from centre O to chord AB.
In isosceles ΔOAB with OA = OB = 21 cm, the altitude OM bisects chord AB and ∠AOB:
∠AOM = ∠BOM = 120° / 2 = 60°,
and AM = BM = AB / 2.
In right triangle ΔOMA:
- OM / OA = cos(60°) ⇒ OM = 21 × (1/2) = 21/2 cm.
- AM / OA = sin(60°) ⇒ AM = 21 × (√3/2) = 21√3 / 2 cm.
Therefore, chord length AB = 2 × AM = 2 × (21√3 / 2) = 21√3 cm.

Factoring out 21/4:

Using √3 ≈ 1.732:

worked_examples.solution:
GIVEN:
Radius of the circle, r = 6 cm.
Angle of the sector, θ = 60°.
Use π = 22/7.

TO FIND:
Area of the sector.

FORMULA USED:
Area of a sector = (θ / 360°) × πr².

STEP-BY-STEP CALCULATION:
Step 1: Substitute the given parameters into the formula:
Area = (60° / 360°) × (22 / 7) × 6²

Step 2: Simplify the angular fraction:
60° / 360° = 1 / 6

Step 3: Perform multiplication:
Area = (1 / 6) × (22 / 7) × 36
Cancel 6 from numerator and denominator:
Area = 6 × (22 / 7) = 132 / 7 cm².
In decimal form: 132 / 7 ≈ 18.86 cm².

[ROUGH_WORK]
(1/6) × 36 = 6. 6 × 22 = 132. 132 / 7 = 18.857... ≈ 18.86 cm².
Boxed Answer: [ 132/7 cm² (or 18.86 cm²) ].

worked_examples.formula: Circumference = 2πr ⇒ r = Circumference / (2π). Area of quadrant = (1/4)πr².
worked_examples.solution:
GIVEN:
Circumference of the circle = 22 cm.
The sector is a quadrant, meaning its central angle θ = 90° (one-fourth of a full circle).
Use π = 22/7.

TO FIND:
Area of the quadrant.

FORMULA USED:
1. Circumference of circle = 2πr
2. Area of a quadrant = (1 / 4) × πr²

STEP-BY-STEP CALCULATION:
Step 1: Calculate the radius r of the circle:
2πr = 22
2 × (22 / 7) × r = 22
(44 / 7) × r = 22
r = (22 × 7) / 44 = 7 / 2 cm = 3.5 cm.

Step 2: Calculate the area of the quadrant:
Area = (1 / 4) × πr²
Area = (1 / 4) × (22 / 7) × (7 / 2)²
Area = (1 / 4) × (22 / 7) × (49 / 4)
Simplify by cancelling 7 into 49 (gives 7) and 2 from 22 (gives 11 and 2):
Area = (11 × 7) / (4 × 2) = 77 / 8 cm².
In decimal representation:
77 / 8 = 9.625 cm².

[ROUGH_WORK]
2πr = 22 ⇒ r = 3.5 cm. Area = (1/4) × π × r² = 0.25 × (22/7) × 12.25 = 0.25 × 38.5 = 9.625 cm².
Boxed Answer: [ 77/8 cm² (or 9.625 cm²) ].

worked_examples.formula: The minute hand completes a full circle (360°) in 60 minutes. Angle swept in 1 minute = 360° / 60 = 6°. Angle in t minutes = t × 6°. Area swept = (θ / 360°) × πr².
worked_examples.solution:
GIVEN:
Length of the minute hand of the clock, r = 14 cm.
Time duration, t = 5 minutes.
Use π = 22/7.

TO FIND:
Area swept by the minute hand in 5 minutes.

FORMULA USED:
- In 60 minutes, the minute hand makes one full 360° revolution.
- Angle swept in 1 minute = 360° / 60 = 6°.
- Angle swept in t minutes: θ = t × 6°.
- Area swept = Area of sector = (θ / 360°) × πr².

STEP-BY-STEP CALCULATION:
Step 1: Determine the angle θ swept in 5 minutes:
θ = 5 × (360° / 60) = 5 × 6° = 30°.

Step 2: Calculate the area of the sector swept:
Area = (θ / 360°) × πr²
Area = (30° / 360°) × (22 / 7) × 14²
Area = (1 / 12) × (22 / 7) × 196
Since 196 / 7 = 28:
Area = (1 / 12) × 22 × 28
Divide 28 and 12 by 4:
Area = (22 × 7) / 3 = 154 / 3 cm².
In decimal representation:
154 / 3 ≈ 51.33 cm².

[ROUGH_WORK]
Fraction of clock = 5/60 = 1/12. Area = (1/12) × (22/7) × 196 = (1/12) × 616 = 154/3 = 51.33 cm².
Boxed Answer: [ 154/3 cm² (or 51.33 cm²) ].

worked_examples.solution:
GIVEN:
Radius of the circle, r = 10 cm.
Central angle subtended by the chord, θ = 90°.
Use π = 3.14.

TO FIND:
(i) Area of the corresponding minor segment.
(ii) Area of the corresponding major sector.

FORMULA USED:
- Area of minor sector = (θ / 360°) × πr²
- Area of right-angled ΔOAB = (1 / 2) × OA × OB = (1 / 2) × r²
- Area of minor segment = Area of minor sector - Area of ΔOAB
- Area of major sector = ((360° - θ) / 360°) × πr²

STEP-BY-STEP CALCULATION:
Part (i): Compute Area of Minor Segment:
1. Area of minor sector:
   = (90° / 360°) × 3.14 × 10²
   = (1 / 4) × 3.14 × 100
   = 314 / 4 = 78.5 cm².
2. Area of right ΔOAB:
   = (1 / 2) × base × height
   = (1 / 2) × 10 × 10 = 50 cm².
3. Area of minor segment:
   = Area of minor sector - Area of ΔOAB
   = 78.5 - 50 = 28.5 cm².

Part (ii): Compute Area of Major Sector:
Angle of major sector = 360° - 90° = 270°.
Area of major sector = (270° / 360°) × πr²
Area = (3 / 4) × 3.14 × 10²
Area = (3 / 4) × 314
Area = 3 × 78.5 = 235.5 cm².
(Alternatively: Area of circle - Area of minor sector = 314 - 78.5 = 235.5 cm²).

[ROUGH_WORK]
Total area = 314 cm². 1/4th circle = 78.5 cm². Triangle = 50 cm². Segment = 78.5 - 50 = 28.5 cm². Major sector = 314 - 78.5 = 235.5 cm².
Boxed Answer: [ (i) Minor segment = 28.5 cm², (ii) Major sector = 235.5 cm² ].

2. Area of sector = (θ / 360°) × πr²

worked_examples.solution:
GIVEN:
Radius of the circle, r = 21 cm.
Central angle, θ = 60°.
Use π = 22/7.

TO FIND:
(i) Length of the arc.
(ii) Area of the sector formed by the arc.
(iii) Area of the segment formed by the corresponding chord.

STEP-BY-STEP CALCULATION:
Part (i): Compute Length of the Arc:
Formula: Arc Length l = (θ / 360°) × 2πr
l = (60° / 360°) × 2 × (22 / 7) × 21
l = (1 / 6) × 2 × 22 × 3
l = (1 / 6) × 132 = 22 cm.

Part (ii): Compute Area of the Sector:
Formula: Area = (θ / 360°) × πr²
Area = (60° / 360°) × (22 / 7) × 21²
Area = (1 / 6) × (22 / 7) × 441
Area = (1 / 6) × 22 × 63
Area = (1 / 6) × 1386 = 231 cm².

Part (iii): Compute Area of the Segment:
In ΔOAB, OA = OB = 21 cm (radii) and ∠AOB = 60°.
Since angles opposite to equal sides are equal: ∠OAB = ∠OBA = (180° - 60°) / 2 = 60°.
Therefore, ΔOAB is an equilateral triangle with side length a = 21 cm.
Area of equilateral ΔOAB = (√3 / 4) × a²
Area(ΔOAB) = (√3 / 4) × 21² = (441√3 / 4) cm².
Now, Area of segment = Area of sector - Area of ΔOAB
Area of segment = 231 - (441√3 / 4) cm².
Using √3 ≈ 1.732:
Area ≈ 231 - (441 × 1.732 / 4) = 231 - 190.95 = 40.05 cm².

[ROUGH_WORK]
Equilateral triangle with side 21: Area = (√3/4) × 441 = 110.25 × 1.732 = 190.953 cm². 231 - 190.95 = 40.05 cm².
Boxed Answer: [ (i) 22 cm, (ii) 231 cm², (iii) (231 - 441√3/4) cm² (or 40.05 cm²) ].

title: Exercise 11.1 Part 2 Solver: 120° Chords, Grazing Horses, Brooches & Umbrellas (Q6 to Q10)
description: Complete step-by-step resolution of NCERT Exercise 11.1 Questions 6 through 10. Covers 15 cm radius 60° chord minor and major segments (Q6), 12 cm radius 120° chord segment (Q7), horse tied to corner of 15 m square field with 5 m and 10 m ropes (Q8), silver wire circular brooch with 10 sectors (Q9), and 8-rib umbrella sector calculation (Q10).

Ex 11.1 Q7: r = 12 cm, θ = 120°: Sector = 150.72 cm²; ΔOAB = (√3/4) × 144 = 62.28 cm² ⇒ Minor segment = 88.44 cm²
Ex 11.1 Q8: Square field corner: Quadrant angle θ = 90°: (i) Grazing area for 5 m rope = 1/4 × 3.14 × 25 = 19.625 m²; (ii) Grazing area for 10 m rope = 78.5 m² ⇒ Increase = 78.5 - 19.625 = 58.875 m²
Ex 11.1 Q9: Brooch diameter 35 mm: Total wire = Circumference + 5 diameters = πd + 5d = (22/7 × 35) + (5 × 35) = 110 + 175 = 285 mm; Sector area = 1/10 × (22/7) × (35/2)² = 385/4 = 96.25 mm²
Ex 11.1 Q10: 8-rib umbrella, radius 45 cm: Angle between consecutive ribs = 360° / 8 = 45° ⇒ Area = (45/360) × (22/7) × 45² = 22275 / 28 cm² = 795.54 cm²
subtopics: Full resolution of Exercise 11.1 Questions 6 to 10
Square corner quadrant geometry and tethered grazing areas
Brooch silver wire total linear length calculation

worked_examples.solution:
GIVEN:
Radius of the circle, r = 12 cm.
Central angle, θ = 120°.
Use π = 3.14 and √3 = 1.73.

TO FIND:
Area of the corresponding segment of the circle.

FORMULA USED:
Area of segment = Area of sector OAB - Area of ΔOAB.
- Area of sector = (θ / 360°) × πr²
- Area of ΔOAB with central angle 120° = (1 / 2) × r² × sin(120°) = (√3 / 4) × r².

STEP-BY-STEP CALCULATION:
Step 1: Compute Area of Sector OAB:
Area of sector = (120° / 360°) × 3.14 × 12²
Area of sector = (1 / 3) × 3.14 × 144
Area of sector = 48 × 3.14 = 150.72 cm².

Step 2: Compute Area of ΔOAB:
Draw altitude OM ⊥ AB from centre O to chord AB.
In right ΔOMA (with ∠AOM = 120°/2 = 60°):
- OM = OA cos(60°) = 12 × (1/2) = 6 cm.
- AM = OA sin(60°) = 12 × (√3/2) = 6√3 cm.
Chord AB = 2 × AM = 2 × 6√3 = 12√3 cm.
Area of ΔOAB = (1 / 2) × base × height
Area of ΔOAB = (1 / 2) × 12√3 × 6 = 36√3 cm².
Substitute √3 = 1.73:
Area of ΔOAB = 36 × 1.73 = 62.28 cm².

Step 3: Compute Area of Segment:
Area of segment = Area of sector - Area of ΔOAB
Area of segment = 150.72 - 62.28 = 88.44 cm².

[ROUGH_WORK]
Sector = 150.72. Triangle = 36 × 1.73 = 62.28. Segment = 150.72 - 62.28 = 88.44 cm².
Boxed Answer: [ 88.44 cm² ].

worked_examples.solution:
GIVEN:
Side of square grass field = 15 m.
Each corner angle of the square field is 90°.
Initial rope length, r1 = 5 m.
Extended rope length, r2 = 10 m.
Use π = 3.14 (Fig. 11.8).

TO FIND:
(i) Area of the field the horse can graze with 5 m rope.
(ii) Increase in grazing area if rope is lengthened to 10 m.

FORMULA USED:
Since the horse is pegged at a 90° corner, the grazing region forms a quadrant (one-fourth) of a circle:
Area of grazing quadrant = (90° / 360°) × πr² = (1 / 4) × πr².

STEP-BY-STEP CALCULATION:
Part (i): Grazing area with 5 m rope:
Area = (1 / 4) × π × r1²
Area = (1 / 4) × 3.14 × 5²
Area = (1 / 4) × 3.14 × 25
Area = 78.5 / 4 = 19.625 m².

Part (ii): Increase in grazing area with 10 m rope:
Grazing area with 10 m rope:
Area_new = (1 / 4) × π × r2²
Area_new = (1 / 4) × 3.14 × 10²
Area_new = (1 / 4) × 3.14 × 100
Area_new = 314 / 4 = 78.5 m².

Increase in grazing area = Area_new - Area_initial
Increase = 78.5 - 19.625 = 58.875 m².
(Alternatively: (1/4) × 3.14 × (100 - 25) = (1/4) × 3.14 × 75 = 235.5 / 4 = 58.875 m²).

[ROUGH_WORK]
(i) 0.25 × 3.14 × 25 = 19.625 m². (ii) 0.25 × 3.14 × 100 = 78.5 m². Difference = 78.5 - 19.625 = 58.875 m².
Boxed Answer: [ (i) 19.625 m², (ii) 58.875 m² ].

worked_examples.solution:
GIVEN:
Diameter of the circular brooch, d = 35 mm.
Radius, r = d / 2 = 35 / 2 mm.
Number of diameters formed with wire = 5.
The brooch is divided into 10 equal sectors (Fig. 11.9).
Use π = 22/7.

TO FIND:
(i) Total length of the silver wire required.
(ii) Area of each of the 10 sectors of the brooch.

STEP-BY-STEP CALCULATION:
Part (i): Compute Total Length of Silver Wire:
The wire is used to form the outer circular circumference plus 5 full diameters:
Total Length = Circumference + 5 × Diameter
Circumference = 2πr = πd = (22 / 7) × 35 = 22 × 5 = 110 mm.
Length of 5 diameters = 5 × 35 = 175 mm.
Total wire required = 110 + 175 = 285 mm.

Part (ii): Compute Area of Each Sector:
Since the circle is divided into 10 equal sectors, the central angle of each sector is:
θ = 360° / 10 = 36°.
Area of each sector = (θ / 360°) × πr²
Area = (1 / 10) × πr²
Area = (1 / 10) × (22 / 7) × (35 / 2) × (35 / 2)
Simplify by cancelling 7 into 35 (giving 5):
Area = (1 / 10) × 22 × 5 × (35 / 4)
Since 22 × 5 = 110 and 110 / 10 = 11:
Area = 11 × (35 / 4) = 385 / 4 mm².

worked_examples.solution:
GIVEN:
An umbrella modeled as a flat circle of radius r = 45 cm.
There are 8 ribs equally spaced, creating 8 equal sectors (Fig. 11.10).
Use π = 22/7.

TO FIND:
Area between two consecutive ribs of the umbrella.

FORMULA USED:
- Angle between two consecutive ribs, θ = 360° / 8 = 45°.
- Area between two consecutive ribs = Area of one sector = (1 / 8) × πr².

STEP-BY-STEP CALCULATION:
Step 1: Compute the fraction of the circle:
Since there are 8 equal sectors, each sector has an area equal to (1 / 8) of the total circular area.

Step 2: Apply the sector area formula:
Area = (1 / 8) × πr²
Area = (1 / 8) × (22 / 7) × 45²
Area = (1 / 8) × (22 / 7) × 2025

Step 3: Simplify by cancelling 2 from 22 and 8:
Area = (11 × 2025) / (4 × 7)
Area = 22275 / 28 cm².
In decimal form:
22275 / 28 ≈ 795.54 cm².

[ROUGH_WORK]
45² = 2025. 2025 × 11 = 22275. Denominator = 4 × 7 = 28. 22275 / 28 = 795.5357... ≈ 795.54 cm².
Boxed Answer: [ 22275/28 cm² (or 795.54 cm²) ].

worked_examples.problem: [NCERT Class 10 Ch 11 | Section 11.1 | Page 159] Exercise 11.1 Q11: A car has two wipers which do not overlap. Each wiper has a blade of length 25 cm sweeping through an angle of 115°. Find the total area cleaned at each sweep of the blades (Use π = 22/7).
worked_examples.section: 11.1 Areas of Sector and Segment of a Circle
worked_examples.image_search_query: car wipers sweeping angle sector area
worked_examples.given: Two non-overlapping blades. Length of each blade r = 25 cm. Sweep angle θ = 115°. Use π = 22/7.
worked_examples.formula: Area swept by 1 blade = (θ / 360°) × πr². Total area swept by 2 blades = 2 × Area of 1 blade.
worked_examples.solution:
GIVEN:
Number of wiper blades = 2 (non-overlapping).
Length of each blade, r = 25 cm.
Angle of sweep for each blade, θ = 115°.
Use π = 22/7.

TO FIND:
Total area cleaned at each sweep of the blades.

FORMULA USED:
Area cleaned by one blade = Area of sector = (θ / 360°) × πr².
Total area cleaned by two identical non-overlapping blades = 2 × (θ / 360°) × πr².

STEP-BY-STEP CALCULATION:
Step 1: Write down the expression for the combined area:
Total Area = 2 × [ (115° / 360°) × (22 / 7) × 25² ]

Step 2: Simplify fractions:
Cancel 2 with 360:
Total Area = (115 / 180) × (22 / 7) × 625
Divide 115 and 180 by 5:
Total Area = (23 / 36) × (22 / 7) × 625
Divide 22 and 36 by 2:
Total Area = (23 / 18) × (11 / 7) × 625

Step 3: Multiply numerators and denominators:
Numerator = 23 × 11 × 625 = 253 × 625 = 158125.
Denominator = 18 × 7 = 126.
Total Area = 158125 / 126 cm².
In decimal representation:
158125 / 126 ≈ 1254.96 cm².

[ROUGH_WORK]
253 × 625 = 158125. 18 × 7 = 126. 158125 / 126 = 1254.9603... ≈ 1254.96 cm².
Boxed Answer: [ 158125/126 cm² (or 1254.96 cm²) ].

What units must the angle and distance be in when computing the illuminated sea area?

worked_examples.problem: [NCERT Class 10 Ch 11 | Section 11.1 | Page 159] Exercise 11.1 Q12: To warn ships for underwater rocks, a lighthouse spreads a red coloured light over a sector of angle 80° to a distance of 16.5 km. Find the area of the sea over which the ships are warned (Use π = 3.14).
worked_examples.section: 11.1 Areas of Sector and Segment of a Circle
worked_examples.given: Sector angle θ = 80°. Distance of spread (radius) r = 16.5 km. Use π = 3.14.
worked_examples.solution:
GIVEN:
Sector angle of light spread, θ = 80°.
Distance over which the light spreads (radius), r = 16.5 km.
Use π = 3.14.

TO FIND:
Area of the sea over which the ships are warned.

FORMULA USED:
Area of the sea warned = Area of sector = (θ / 360°) × πr².

STEP-BY-STEP CALCULATION:
Step 1: Substitute the given values into the sector formula:
Area = (80° / 360°) × 3.14 × (16.5)²

Step 2: Simplify the angular fraction:
80° / 360° = 8 / 36 = 2 / 9.

Step 3: Compute (16.5)²:
16.5 × 16.5 = 272.25.

Step 4: Divide 272.25 by 9:
272.25 / 9 = 30.25.

Step 5: Multiply the remaining factors:
Area = 2 × 3.14 × 30.25
Area = 6.28 × 30.25 = 189.97 km².

[ROUGH_WORK]
(2/9) × 3.14 × 272.25 = 2 × 3.14 × 30.25 = 6.28 × 30.25 = 189.97 km².
Boxed Answer: [ 189.97 km² ].

worked_examples.formula:
Central angle for each of 6 equal designs θ = 360° / 6 = 60°.
Area of 1 design = Area of minor segment = Area of sector (60°) - Area of equilateral ΔOAB.
Area of 6 designs = 6 × [ ((60/360) × πr²) - ((√3/4) × r²) ].
Cost = Total Design Area × Rate.

Cost = 464.8 × 0.35 = ₹ 162.68.
worked_examples.solution:
GIVEN:
Radius of the round table cover, r = 28 cm.
Number of equal designs = 6 (arranged along the circumference as circular segments, Fig. 11.11).
Cost rate = ₹ 0.35 per cm².
Use √3 = 1.7 and π = 22/7.

TO FIND:
Total cost of making the 6 designs.

STEP-BY-STEP CALCULATION:
Step 1: Determine the central angle of each design segment:
Since the cover has 6 equal designs forming a regular hexagonal boundary:
θ = 360° / 6 = 60°.

Step 2: Area of one sector of 60°:
Area of 1 sector = (60° / 360°) × πr²
Area = (1 / 6) × (22 / 7) × 28²
Area = (1 / 6) × (22 / 7) × 784
Since 784 / 7 = 112:
Area = (22 × 112) / 6 = 2464 / 6 cm².

Step 3: Area of one equilateral triangle ΔOAB:
In ΔOAB, OA = OB = 28 cm and ∠AOB = 60°, so ΔOAB is equilateral:
Area(ΔOAB) = (√3 / 4) × r²
Area(ΔOAB) = (1.7 / 4) × 28²
Area(ΔOAB) = (1.7 / 4) × 784 = 1.7 × 196 = 333.2 cm².

Step 4: Area of one design (segment):
Area of 1 design = Area of 1 sector - Area of ΔOAB
Area of 1 design = (2464 / 6) - 333.2 cm².

Step 5: Total Area of all 6 designs:
Total Area = 6 × [ (2464 / 6) - 333.2 ]
Total Area = 2464 - (6 × 333.2)
Total Area = 2464 - 1999.2 = 464.8 cm².

Step 6: Compute the total cost:
Cost = Total Area × Rate
Cost = 464.8 × ₹ 0.35 = ₹ 162.68.

6 sectors = full circle area = (22/7) × 784 = 2464 cm². 6 triangles = 6 × 333.2 = 1999.2 cm². Design area = 2464 - 1999.2 = 464.8 cm². Cost = 464.8 × 0.35 = ₹ 162.68.
Boxed Answer: [ ₹ 162.68 ].

(C) (p / 360) × 2πR
(D) (p / 720) × 2πR²
worked_examples.section: 11.1 Areas of Sector and Segment of a Circle
worked_examples.given: Angle of sector = p (in degrees). Radius of circle = R.
worked_examples.substitution: Replace θ by p: Area = (p / 360) × πR² = (p / (360 × 2)) × (2 × πR²) = (p / 720) × 2πR².
worked_examples.calculation:
Option (A) is (p/180) × 2πR = arc length with halved denominator (incorrect).
Option (B) is (p/180) × πR² (incorrect denominator).
Option (C) is (p/360) × 2πR = arc length, not area (incorrect).
Option (D) is (p/720) × 2πR² = (p / 360) × πR² (correct).
worked_examples.solution:
GIVEN:
A circle with radius R and a sector with angle of measure p degrees.

TO FIND:
The correct algebraic expression for the area of the sector among the given options.

FORMULA USED:
The area of a sector of angle θ in a circle of radius r is:
Area = (θ / 360) × πr².

STEP-BY-STEP CALCULATION:
Step 1: Substitute the given parameters θ = p and r = R:
Area = (p / 360) × πR²   ... (1)

Step 2: Evaluate the given options against expression (1):
- Option (A): (p / 180) × 2πR = (p / 90) × πR (Dimension of length, represents twice arc length, incorrect)
- Option (B): (p / 180) × πR² (Incorrect denominator; would represent a sector of a circle with 180° full turn)
- Option (C): (p / 360) × 2πR (Dimension of length, represents the arc length of the sector, not area)
- Option (D): (p / 720) × 2πR²
Multiply and divide by 2 in equation (1):
Area = (p / (360 × 2)) × (2 × πR²) = (p / 720) × 2πR².
This matches Option (D) identically!

Therefore, option (D) is the correct answer.

[ROUGH_WORK]
(p / 720) × 2πR² = (2 / 720) × pπR² = (1 / 360) × pπR² = (p / 360) × πR².
Boxed Answer: [ (p / 720) × 2πR² (Option D) ].

Area of Shaded Flower Design = Area of Square - Area of 4 unshaded corner regions.
worked_examples.substitution:
Area of Square = 14 × 14 = 196 cm².
Area of 2 semicircles = Area of 1 full circle = πr² = (22/7) × 7² = 154 cm².

Area of all 4 unshaded regions = 2 × 42 = 84 cm².
Area of shaded design = 196 - 84 = 112 cm².
worked_examples.solution:
GIVEN:
A square ABCD of side length a = 14 cm.
Four semicircles are drawn inside the square taking each of the four sides AB, BC, CD, and DA as diameter.
Diameter of each semicircle = 14 cm ⇒ radius, r = 7 cm.
Use π = 22/7.

TO FIND:
Area of the four shaded petals/leaves formed in the interior of the square.

FORMULA USED:
- Area of square = a²
- Area of semicircle = (1/2)πr²
- Two semicircles combined = One full circle of radius r = πr²
- Area of shaded design = Area of square - Area of 4 unshaded corner regions.

STEP-BY-STEP CALCULATION:
Step 1: Compute Area of Square ABCD:
Area_square = 14 × 14 = 196 cm².

Step 2: Calculate area of unshaded corner regions:
Let the four unshaded corner regions be marked I, II, III, and IV.
Consider the pair of semicircles drawn on opposite sides AB and CD as diameters:
Sum of areas of these two semicircles = 2 × [(1/2)πr²] = πr² = (22 / 7) × 7² = 154 cm².
The remaining area in the square when these two semicircles are removed consists of regions I and III:
Area(I + III) = Area_square - Area of two semicircles
Area(I + III) = 196 - 154 = 42 cm².
By identical symmetry for semicircles on sides AD and BC:
Area(II + IV) = 196 - 154 = 42 cm².
Total area of all 4 unshaded regions = Area(I + III) + Area(II + IV) = 42 + 42 = 84 cm².

Step 3: Compute Area of Shaded Petal Design:
Area of shaded design = Area_square - Total unshaded area
Area of shaded design = 196 - 84 = 112 cm².

[ROUGH_WORK]
Sum of 4 semicircles = 2 × 154 = 308 cm². Each shaded petal is counted twice: Area_shaded = 308 - 196 = 112 cm²!
Boxed Answer: [ 112 cm² ].
